Type.Name: IAngleMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to an angle mate or a limit angle mate feature.

Example.Name: Create and Edit Limit Angle Mate
Create and Edit Limit Angle Mate

Type.Remarks:
An angle mate places selected items at a specified angle. A limit angle mate is an advanced mate that allows items to move within a range of angles. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAngleMateFeatureData.IsAdvancedMate">IAngleMateFeatureData::IsAdvancedMate</see> to determine whether this is a limit angle mate.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create either an angle mate or a limit angle mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAngleMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">IAngleMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1.
3. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAngleMateFeatureData.ReferenceEntity">IAngleMateFeatureData::ReferenceEntity</see> or use IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 to pre-select the reference entity using Mark = 67108864.
4. Specify other properties of the AngleMateFeatureData object.
To edit an angle mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to an AngleMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the AngleMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this angle mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Name: IAnnotation
Type.Description: Allows access to notes, weld symbols, datum tags, display dimensions, blocks, cosmetic threads, center marks, centerlines, and other annotation types.

Example.Name: Get Whether Note Contains Rich-embedded Text
Get DimXpert Display Dimensions and Feature
Get DimXpert Display Dimensions and Feature
Get DimXpert Display Dimensions and Feature

Type.Remarks:
Because IAnnotation is a high-level representation of all annotation types, it provides functions that are generic to all types of annotations. For example, every annotation has a name and position, so IAnnotation provides functions that access this data.
Although IAnnotation has specific lower-level objects (such as <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.INote">INote</see>), it does not have any derived classes in the SOLIDWORKS API. This means that you cannot use an IAnnotation pointer to call functions in the lower-level objects. You also cannot use QueryInterface to obtain the underlying classes. Instead, SOLIDWORKS provides <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.IGetSpecificAnnotation">IAnnotation::GetSpecificAnnotation</see>, which accesses underlying objects.
Similarly if you are holding onto a lower-level class, then you can obtain the corresponding IAnnotation object using the GetAnnotation method of that class (see the **Accessors** list in this topic).

Type.Name: IAttribute
Type.Description: Allows access to an attribute's values.

Example.Name: Add Attribute to Feature and Include in Library Feature
Add Attribute to Feature and Include in Library Feature
Add Attribute to Feature and Include in Library Feature

Type.Remarks:
An attribute is a piece of information that can be stored on a <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IBody2">body</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2">component</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEntity">entity</see> ( <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edge</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IVertex">vertex</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ILoop2">loop2</see>, or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">feature</see>), and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">model</see> if null.
After you place an attribute on an object, you can get the IAttribute object and get or set its parameter values. For example, you can place an attribute containing NC machining information on a face. You can then use that attribute in automation on the shop floor to know what feed or speed to use during the machining process.
You can also add attributes to a <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2">document object</see>.
From the attribute instance you can get the:
- Attribute definition
- Associated entity
- Parameter values
- Instance name

Type.Name: IAttributeDef
Type.Description: Allows access to an attribute definition.

Example.Name: Add Attribute to Feature and Include in Library Feature
Add Attribute to Feature and Include in Library Feature
Add Attribute to Feature and Include in Library Feature

Type.Remarks:
An attribute definition is an application-specific data packet that is automatically saved with the SOLIDWORKS file and reloaded when the file is opened. An application can create <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAttribute">attribute</see> data that is attached to an entity in a SOLIDWORKS document.
The attribute definition describes a template for the data packet. The definition contains the names of the parameters in the attribute, their types and default values. It also allows you to create instances of the definition on entities in your model.
The general sequence of steps in IAttribute creation is to:
1. Create an attribute definition (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.DefineAttribute">ISldWorks::DefineAttribute</see>)
2. Add parameters to the attribute definition (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAttributeDef.AddParameter">IAttributeDef::AddParameter</see>)
3. Register the attribute definition (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAttributeDef.Register">IAttributeDef::Register</see>)
4. Create instances of the attribute definition on objects throughout the model (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAttributeDef.CreateInstance5">IAttributeDef::CreateInstance5</see>)
Perform Steps 1 through 3 only once for each working session. In other words, perform Steps 1 through 3 when your DLL or EXE is initially loaded or run. Until the DLL is unloaded or the EXE is closed, you can create an unlimited number of instances of the attribute definition.

Type.Name: ICamFollowerMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a cam-follower mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A cam-follower mate:
- Allows you to mate a cylinder, plane, or point on a cam-follower part to the tangent faces of a cam part.
- Appears in the FeatureManager design tree as either CamMateCoincident or CamMateTangent.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a cam-follower mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICamFollowerMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">ICamFollowerMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> for each EntityType or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1 for the cam face and Mark = 8 for the cam-follower face or vertex.
3. Specify other properties of the CamFollowerMateFeatureData object.
To edit a cam-follower mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a CamFollowerMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the CamFollowerMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this cam-follower mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Get and Set Center Mark Set

Type.Remarks:
Center marks are now annotations. Previously, center marks were features.
Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICenterMark.GetAnnotation">ICenterMark::GetAnnotation</see> to access the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation">IAnnotation</see> APIs. If you use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObject6">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObject6</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObjectType3">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObjectType3</see> to retrieve center marks, then these values are returned:
- swSelCENTERMARKSSYMS = 100 for the center marks that are annotations
- swSelCENTERMARKS = 28 for the center marks that are features
Both methods retrieve the ICenterMark object.
**To...**
**Use...**
Traverse center marks that are annotations
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetFirstAnnotation3">IView::GetFirstAnnotation3</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.GetNext3">IAnnotation::GetNext3</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetFirstCenterMark">IView::GetFirstCenterMark</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICenterMark.GetNext">ICenterMark::GetNext</see>
Retrieve center marks that are features
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetCenterMarkCount2">IView::GetCenterMarkCount2</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IView.GetCenterMarks">IView::GetCenterMarks</see>
Center marks are displayed using the document's default display attribute settings. If you want the setting to be local to this symbol, then set the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICenterMark.UseDocDisplaySettings">ICenterMark::UseDocDisplaySettings</see> property to false and modify the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICenterMark.ShowLines">ICenterMark::ShowLines</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICenterMark.Size">ICenterMark::Size</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ICenterMark.CenterLineFont">ICenterMark::CenterLineFont</see> properties as needed.
A center mark set is a linear or circular pattern.

Type.Name: ICoincidentMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a coincident mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A coincident mate:
- Positions the selected faces, edges, and planes so they share the same infinite plane.
- Positions two vertices so they touch.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a coincident mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICoincidentMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">ICoincidentMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities to mate using Mark = 1.
3. Specify other properties of the CoincidentMateFeatureData object.
To edit a coincident mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a CoincidentMateFeatureData object.
3. You cannot change the entities to mate by pre-selection. You must use ICoincidentMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate to modify them.
4. Modify other properties of the CoincidentMateFeatureData object.
5. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this coincident mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Name: ICollisionDetectionManager
Type.Description: Allows access to the collision detection manager.
Type.Remarks:
The purpose of this interface, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICollisionDetectionGroup">ICollisionDetectionGroup</see>, and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICollision">ICollision</see> is to provide dynamic, high-efficiency collision detection among groups of components. Collision detection is performed exclusively between collision groups: neither within collision groups nor outside of them.
Please use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IInterferenceDetectionMgr">IInterferenceDetectionMgr</see> if you need to perform static interference detection between components.
Collision detection may be thought of as a series of collision detection frames. Each collision detection frame begins by setting a target assembly and two or more collision groups of components that are transformed to move to precise locations in model space. A collision detection frame may or may not end with a collision.
**NOTE**: If a collision is detected, an ICollision object is created. Be aware that ICollision objects are volatile and should not be cached for later review. ICollision objects are invalidated when a new collision detection frame begins or whenever you:
- call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICollisionDetectionManager.IsCollisionPresent">ICollisionDetectionManager::IsCollisionPresent</see>.
- call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICollisionDetectionManager.GetCollisions">ICollisionDetectionManager::GetCollisions</see>.
- apply new transforms to collision group components.
- create new or modify existing collision groups.
- set a new target assembly.
Because you cannot save ICollision objects for later review, you should record the collision detection frame setup and any resulting collision components and transforms before the next collision detection frame begins.
The workflow to detect collisions:
1. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICollisionDetectionManager.SetAssembly">ICollisionDetectionManager::SetAssembly</see> to set the target assembly for collision detection.
2. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICollisionDetectionManager.CreateGroup">ICollisionDetectionManager::CreateGroup</see> to create two collision groups.
3. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICollisionDetectionGroup.SetComponents">ICollisionDetectionGroup::SetComponents</see> to populate each collision group.
4. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICollisionDetectionGroup.ApplyTransforms">ICollisionDetectionGroup::ApplyTransforms</see> to transform components into working positions.
5. Call ICollisionDetectionManager::IsCollisionPresent and/or ICollisionDetectionManager::GetCollisions to detect collisions.
6. Inspect any resulting ICollision objects. (See the NOTE above.)
7. Repeat steps 4-6 if you want to apply new transforms for the next collision detection frame.
8. Repeat steps 2-6 if you want to change collision groups.
9. Repeat steps 1-6 if you want to change the target assembly.

Type.Name: IComplexCornerTreatmentFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a complex corner treatment feature of a structure system.
Type.Remarks:
This interface is:
- derived from <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerTreatmentFeatureData">ICornerTreatmentFeatureData</see>.
- valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerTreatmentFeatureData.IgnoreCornerTreatment">ICornerTreatmentFeatureData::IgnoreCornerTreatment</see> is false.
A complex corner is the position in a structure system where three or more members intersect.
In the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface, the Complex Corner PropertyManager contains five lists that you can manage using the APIs in this interface and elsewhere:
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerTreatmentGroupFolder.GetCornerTreatments">Corner groups</see>
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IComplexCornerTreatmentFeatureData.GetTrimToolMember">Trim tool</see> member
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IComplexCornerTreatmentFeatureData.GetBodyTrimMembers">Body trim</see> members
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IComplexCornerTreatmentFeatureData.GetPlanarTrimMembers">Planar trim</see> members
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IComplexCornerTreatmentFeatureData.UserDefinedTrimFaces">User defined trim</see> faces
You can assign one member as a trim tool and use it to add or remove material from adjacent members. Other members are trimmed based on their designated trim orders and positions with respect to touching members.
For more information, see:
- **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Weldments and Structure System > Structure System > Corner Management > Trimming Complex Corners**
- ****SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Weldments and Structure System > Structure System > Corner Management > Examples of Complex Corner Management****
- **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Weldments and Structure System > Structure System > Complex Corner PropertyManager**

Type.Name: IConvertSolidFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a convert solid feature.
Type.Remarks:
To create a ConvertSolid feature:
1. Ensure that the Sheet Metal tab is visible on the CommandManager toolbar.
2. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select the fixed face (with Mark=0) and bend edges (with Mark=1).

4. Instantiate and specify the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICustomBendAllowance">ICustomBendAllowance</see> object.
5. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IConvertSolidFeatureData.Initialize">IConvertSolidFeatureData::Initialize</see>.
6. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see> to create the ConvertSolid feature.
To modify a ConvertSolid feature:
1. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to obtain this feature data object.
2. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IConvertSolidFeatureData.AccessSelections">IConvertSolidFeatureData::AccessSelections</see>.
3. Modify properties as needed.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> to finalize any changes or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IConvertSolidFeatureData.ReleaseSelectionAccess">IConvertSolidFeatureData::ReleaseSelectionAccess</see> if no changes were made.
For more information about converting solids or surface bodies to sheet metal parts, see the **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface online help > Sheet Metal > Comparing Sheet Metal Design Methods > Convert to Sheet Metal Tool** topics.

Type.Name: ICoordinateSystemElement
Type.Description: Allows access to a coordinate system element.
Type.Remarks:
The normal channel of feature editing (IFeature::CreateDefinition, IFeature::ModifyDefinition) will not work for features created with coordinate system elements. In order to edit a feature created with a coordinate system element, you must:
1. Select the feature created with a coordinate system element.
2. Call the IModelDocExtension::RunCommand swCommands_e.swCommands_EditFeature to open a PropertyManager dialog for the selected object.
3. Call ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObjectType3 to obtain the selection.
4. Test whether the selection is a coordinate system element.
5. If the selection is a coordinate system element, obtain the CoordinateSystemElement object.
'VBA
'--------------------------------------------------------------------- ' Preconditions: ' 1. Open a part that contains an Axis1 created using a coordinate system element. ' 2. Open the Immediate window. ' ' Postconditions: ' 1. Examine the Immediate window to see the coordinate system element type as defined by swCoordSysElementType_e. ' 2. Examine the user interface. The specified coordinate system element should be selected. ' '--------------------------------------------------------------------- Option Explicit Dim swApp As SldWorks.SldWorks Dim swModel As SldWorks.ModelDoc2 Dim swSelMgr As SldWorks.SelectionMgr Dim iSelType As Long Dim isCoordSysElmSelected As Boolean Dim swCordSysElement As SldWorks.CoordinateSystemElement Dim boolstatus As Boolean
Sub main()
Set swApp = Application.SldWorks
Set swModel = swApp.ActiveDoc boolstatus = swModel.Extension.SelectByID2("Axis1", "AXIS", 0, 0, 0, False, 0, Nothing, 0) swModel.Extension.RunCommand swCommands_e.swCommands_EditFeature, ""
Set swSelMgr = swModel.SelectionManager iSelType = swSelMgr.GetSelectedObjectType3(1, -1)
If iSelType = swSelCOORDSYS Then
isCoordSysElmSelected = swSelMgr.IsCoordSysElementSelected(1, -1)
If isCoordSysElmSelected Then
Set swCordSysElement = swSelMgr.GetSelectedCoordSysElement(1, -1) Debug.Print "Element type: " & swCordSysElement.GetElementType
End If
End If swModel.Extension.RunCommand swCommands_e.swCommands_Dve_Rmb_Cancel, "" Set swCordSysElement = Nothing
End Sub

In your application, the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICustomBendAllowance.Type">ICustomBendAllowance::Type</see> must always be set last, after the other properties of this interface have been set. The property last set automically overrides any previously set ICustomBendAllowance::Type.
For example:
cba.**Type** = swBendAllowanceTypes_e.swBendAllowanceDeduction '***set first, so will not hold***
'***RESET THE VALUES***
cba.**KFactor** = 0.08
cba.**BendDeduction** = 0.1
cba.**BendAllowance** = 0.11
cba.**BendTableFile** = "E:\AAA Projects\sw2025\QA\SP02\Convert To Sheetmetal FUN156195\1-Staal.xls"
cba.**BendCalculationTableFile** = "E:\AAA Projects\sw2025\QA\SP02\Convert To Sheetmetal FUN156195\1-Staal.xls"
**cba.Type = swBendAllowanceTypes_e.swBendAllowanceDirect '***set last, so holds******
**The above code sets the ICustomBendAllowance::Type as swBendAllowanceTypes_e.swBendAllowanceDirect.**
Another example:
cba.**Type** = swBendAllowanceTypes_e.swBendAllowanceDeduction '***set first, so will not hold***
'***RESET THE VALUES***
cba.**KFactor** = 0.08
cba.**BendDeduction** = 0.1
cba.**BendAllowance** = 0.11
cba.**BendTableFile** = "E:\AAA Projects\sw2025\QA\SP02\Convert To Sheetmetal FUN156195\1-Staal.xls"
cba.**BendCalculationTableFile** = "E:\AAA Projects\sw2025\QA\SP02\Convert To Sheetmetal FUN156195\1-Staal.xls"
**‘cba.**Type **= swBendAllowanceTypes_e.swBendAllowanceDirect '***set last would hold**** BUT COMMENTED OUT**
**The above code sets the ICustomBendAllowance::Type as swBendAllowanceTypes_e.swBendAllowanceBendCalculationTable, because the last property set was BendCalculationTableFile.**
The last ICustomBendAllowance property that is set automatically re-sets the type of bend allowance. You can always explicitly specify the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICustomBendAllowance.Type">ICustomBendAllowance::Type</see>, but you must set it after all other properties of this interface have been set.

Type.Name: IDSPBRMaterial
Type.Description: Allows access to Dassault Systemes Physically Based Rendering (DSPBR) material object.
Type.Remarks:
The Enterprise PBR Shading Model (DSPBR) is a high-quality, easy-to-use material optimized for performance in real-time and interactive scenarios, suitable for rasterization and ray tracing. Inspired by the Disney Principled BRDF and the Unreal Shading Model, it combines a metallic and a dielectric bidirectional scattering distribution function (BSDF), including transparency for thin-walled and volumetric objects. In addition, it provides effects like emission, clear coat, metallic flakes and sheen to cover a wide range of appearances.
For the DSPBR design rationale and detailed mathematical description in terms of BSDF and related concepts, open https://dassaultsystemes-technology.github.io/EnterprisePBRShadingModel/spec-2025x.md.html in an internet browser.
The properties in IDSPBRMaterial map to the appearance settings in the user interface, if the DSPBR appearance is activated in the user interface.
To activate the DSPBR appearance in the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface:
1. Select **System Options > Display > Appearance Visual Style > DSPBR (Dassault Systemes Physically Based Rendering)**.
2. Open a model.
3. Select MMGS in the unit system dropdown below the graphics area.
4. Click **Edit Appearance** in the graphics toolbar.
5. Click the **DSPBR** tab in the FeatureManager.
6. Select **Enerprise PBR Shading Model** from the DSPBR Appearance Type dropdown.

Before calling IFeatureManager::CreateDefinition, you must pre-select the entities needed to create the derived pattern feature. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select the seed components and pattern feature in any order using Marks:

**NOTE**: A derived pattern feature is also called a pattern driven pattern feature.
For more information, see the **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Assemblies > Basic Component Operations > Component Patterns > Pattern Driven Component Pattern PropertyManager** topic.

Type.Name: IDimXpertTolerance
Type.Description: Allows you to access DimXpert geometric tolerance information for annotations on the DimXpertManager tab of the Management Panel.

Example.Name: Get DimXpert Features and Annotations Example

Type.Remarks:
DimXpert geometric tolerance annotations are configured by clicking the Geometric Tolerance icon on the DimXpert tool bar and entering information in the Geometric Tolerance Properties dialog. This interface accesses the tolerances, datums, and datum modifiers that are set in this dialog.
Use this interface to obtain circularity, cylindricity, circular runout, and total runout tolerance data. This interface is also the base class for several more specific interfaces (see **See Also** section below). You can access more general annotation information using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swdimxpert.IDimXpertAnnotation">IDimXpertAnnotation</see>. Use the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swdimxpert.IDimXpertAnnotation.Type">IDimXpertAnnotation::Type</see> property to find out which specific interface is needed to acquire more information for a given tolerance type.

Type.Name: IDisplayDimension
Type.Description: Represents instances of dimensions displayed in <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc">parts</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc">assemblies</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc">drawings</see> and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISensor">sensors</see>.

Example.Name: Get DimXpert Display Dimensions and Feature
Get DimXpert Display Dimensions and Feature
Get DimXpert Display Dimensions and Feature
Set Properties of Angular Running Dimension
Set Properties of Angular Running Dimension
Set Properties of Angular Running Dimension

Type.Remarks:
You can display a SOLIDWORKS dimension more than once. For example, you can bring the base-extrude dimension into three different views on a drawing. These three dimensions are referred to as display dimensions and are represented by the DisplayDimension object in the SOLIDWORKS API. The original base-extrude dimension is represented by the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDimension">Dimension</see> object in the SOLIDWORKS API.
SOLIDWORKS stores many of the properties associated with a dimension with the underlying Dimension object. For example, you must get the Dimension object using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayDimension.GetDimension">IDisplayDimension::GetDimension</see> to access or modify the underlying dimension value.

Type.Name: IDisplayStateSetting
Type.Description: Allows access to display state settings.

Example.Name: Change Color of Component in Specific Display State
Change Color of Component in Specific Display State
Change Color of Component in Specific Display State

Type.Remarks:
After accessing this interface:
1. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayStateSetting.Names">IDisplayStateSetting::Names</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayStateSetting.ISetNames">IDisplayStateSetting::ISetNames</see> to specify the display states.
2. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayStateSetting.Entities">IDisplayStateSetting::Entities</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayStateSetting.ISetEntities">IDisplayStateSetting::ISetEntities</see> to specify the entities.
3. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDisplayStateSetting.Option">IDisplayStateSetting::Option</see> to specify the display state scope of the setting.
4. Get or set one or more of the following properties for the specified display states, entities, and scope:
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DisplayMode">IModelDocExtension::DisplayMode</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.Transparency">IModelDocExtension::Transparency</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.Visibility">IModelDocExtension::Visibility</see>
5. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetAppearanceSetting">IModelDocExtension::GetAppearanceSetting</see> to obtain an <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAppearanceSetting">IAppearanceSetting</see> object.
6. Set the properties in the IAppearanceSetting object.
7. Get or set the material properties for the specified display states, entities, and scope using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DisplayStateSpecMaterialPropertyValues">IModelDocExtension::DisplayStateSpecMaterialPropertyValues</see>.

Type.Name: IDistanceMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a distance mate or a limit distance mate feature.

Example.Name: Create and Edit Limit Distance Mate
Create and Edit Limit Distance Mate

Type.Remarks:
A distance mate places selected items at a specified distance. A limit distance mate is an advanced mate that allows components to move within a range of distances. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IDistanceMateFeatureData.IsAdvancedMate">IDistanceMateFeatureData::IsAdvancedMate</see> to determine whether this is a limit distance mate.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create either a distance mate or a limit distance mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IDistanceMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">IDistanceMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1.
3. Specify other properties of the DistanceMateFeatureData object.
To edit a distance mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a DistanceMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the DistanceMateFeatureData object.

Type.Remarks:
In Microsoft Visual Studio 2008/MFC 9.0 or later, Microsoft added a new interface called IEntity. Your add-in might not compile if it uses both this interface and the SOLIDWORKS IEntity interface.
Possible errors are:
- error C3121: cannot change GUID for class 'IEntity'
- error C2011: 'IEntity' : 'struct' type redefinition
- undefined symbol errors when linking add-ins that do a QueryInterface on IEntity
To avoid errors, you can:
- Include the namespace when declaring an IEntity variable:
SldWorks::IEntity ent
- Rename IEntity by adding the rename function to the import of **sldworks.tlb**: #import "sldworks.tlb" rename("IEntity", "SWEntity")
and do any of the following:
- use SWEntity instead of IEntity in your code
- do a QueryInterface using the GUID constant of the renamed interface:
pFace->QueryInterface(**IID_SWEntity**, (LPVOID*)&entity);
- do a QueryInterface using a GUID lookup of the renamed interface:
pFace->QueryInterface**(__uuidof(SWEntity),** (LPVOID*)&entity);

Type.Name: IExplodeStep
Type.Description: Allows access to an explode step in the explode view of the active assembly configuration.
Type.Remarks:
This interface is valid only for assemblies. To access the explode steps of an explode view of multibody parts, see <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPartExplodeStep">IPartExplodeStep</see>.
If this is a subassembly explode step, then you can call only one method on this interface, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IExplodeStep.GetSubAssemblyExplodeSteps">IExplodeStep::GetSubAssemblyExplodeSteps</see>, to retrieve the nested explode steps of this subassembly explode step.
The setter properties and methods of this interface:
- Always clear selection lists.
- Do not work if the Explode PropertyManager is open.
- Do not work if any component is being edited in the context of the assembly.
To edit an explode step that is not a subassembly explode step:
1. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IConfigurationManager.ActiveConfiguration">IConfigurationManager::ActiveConfiguration</see> to get the active configuration of the assembly.
2. Access the explode step. See the **Accessors** section.
3. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select:
1. Components to move with Mark = 1.
2. An explode direction entity (cylindrical <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see>, conical face, linear <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edge</see>, or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRefAxis">axis</see>) with Mark = 2 (regular explode steps) or Mark = 34 (radial explode steps).
3. A rotation axis with Mark = 32, if RotateAboutOrigin is set to false (regular explode steps only).
4. A diverge direction entity with Mark = 64 (radial explode steps only).
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObject6">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObject6</see> to get the components selected in step 3a.
5. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IExplodeStep.SetComponents">IExplodeStep::SetComponents</see>, passing in the components gotten in step 4.
6. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IExplodeStep.SetExplodeDirection">IExplodeStep::SetExplodeDirection</see>, passing in the explode direction entity that was selected in step 3b. See **Notes**.
7. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IExplodeStep.SetRotationAxis">IExplodeStep::SetRotationAxis</see>, passing in the rotation axis that was selected in step 3c (for regular explode steps only).
8. Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IExplodeStep.DivergeDirection">IExplodeStep::DivergeDirection</see> to the diverge direction entity that was selected in step 3d (for radial explode steps only). See **Notes**.
9. Modify other explode step properties.
**Notes**:
When editing the object entity for the explode direction or rotation axis, please bear in mind:
If... Then...
Both object and manipulator index are valid Both object and manipulator index are set.
Manipulator index is valid, but object is invalid Manipulator index is set, and object is unchanged.
Object is valid, but manipulator index is invalid
Object is set, but the manipulator index is reset to:
- Z direction index for explode direction.
- XY ring index for rotation axis.
Both object and manipulator index are invalid No values change.
When editing the diverge direction object entity or the diverge from axis flag, please bear in mind:
If... Then...
Diverge direction object is valid IExplodeStep::DivergeDirection properly sets the diverge direction, and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IExplodeStep.DivergeFromAxis">IExplodeStep::DivergeFromAxis</see> is set to true.
Diverge direction object is null IExplodeStep::DivergeDirection is set to null, and IExplodeStep::DivergeFromAxis is set to false.
Diverge direction object is invalid Direction object entity is unchanged.
IExplodeStep::DivergeFromAxis is set to false IExplodeStep::DivergeFromAxis is set to false, and the diverge direction object is set to null.
IExplodeStep::DivergeFromAxis is set to true No values change.

Type.Name: IExportPdfData
Type.Description:
Allows access to the PDF export data interface, which allows you to save:
- one or more drawing sheets to PDF.
- parts and assemblies to 3D PDF.
Type.Remarks:
**To export one or more drawing sheets to PDF:**
1. Get the IExportPdfData object using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.GetExportFileData">ISldWorks::GetExportFileData</see>.
2. Set the sheets to export to PDF using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IExportPdfData.SetSheets">IExportPdfData::SetSheets</see>.
3. Set whether to view the PDF after saving using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IExportPdfData.ViewPdfAfterSaving">IExportPdfData::ViewPdfAfterSaving</see>.
4. Save the sheets using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SaveAs">IModelDocExtension::SaveAs</see>.
**To export a part or assembly to 3D PDF:**
1. Get the IExportPdfData object using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.GetExportFileData">ISldWorks::GetExportFileData</see>.
2. Set <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IExportPdfData.ExportAs3D">IExportPdfData::ExportAs3D</see> to true.
3. Set whether to view the PDF after saving using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IExportPdfData.ViewPdfAfterSaving">IExportPdfData::ViewPdfAfterSaving</see>.
4. Save the part or assembly using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SaveAs">IModelDocExtension::SaveAs</see>.

Type.Name: IFillPatternFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a fill pattern feature.
Type.Remarks:
Read <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/Pattern_Features_and_their_Feature_Data_Objects.htm">Pattern Features and their Feature Data Objects</see>.
Before calling IFeatureManager::CreateDefinition, you must pre-select the entities needed to create the fill pattern feature.
Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select... For the Fill Pattern's... Using Mark...
Sketch, face, planar curve on a face, or coplanar faces Fill boundary
16384
Direction reference (e.g., edge or axis) Pattern direction (if not selected, SOLIDWORKS chooses a direction reference appropriate for the specified layout)
1
Vertex or sketch point Location of the pattern seed instance (if a point is not selected, the pattern seed instance is placed at the center of the fill boundary region)
3
Features Pattern objects 4
Faces Pattern objects 5
Bodies Pattern objects 6
After calling IFeatureManager::CreateDefinition, you can explicitly set other properties on the feature data object. You can also initialize:
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFillPatternFeatureData.PatternLayoutType">IFillPatternFeatureData::PatternLayoutType</see>
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFillPatternFeatureData.LayoutSpacingType">IFillPatternFeatureData::LayoutSpacingType</see>
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFillPatternFeatureData.FeaturesToPatternType">IFillPatternFeatureData::FeaturesToPatternType</see>
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFillPatternFeatureData.GeometryPattern">IFillPatternFeatureData::GeometryPattern</see>
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFillPatternFeatureData.LoopSpacing">IFillPatternFeatureData::LoopSpacing</see> (for all PatternLayoutTypes except <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swPatternLayoutType_e">swPatternLayoutType_e</see>.swPatternLayoutPerforation)
- Depending on the settings above, other properties might need to be initialized.
You must call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see> after initializing this feature data object in order to successfully create the fill pattern feature.
For all pattern layouts except swPatternLayoutType_e.swPatternLayoutPerforation, the fill pattern is created by positioning a pattern seed instance within the fill boundary and copying the pattern in concentric loops about the seed instance.
See the **Fill Pattern PropertyManager** topic in the SOLIDWORKS Help for more information about fill pattern features.

Type.Name: IGearMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to gear mate features.
Type.Remarks:
A gear mate forces two components to rotate relative to one another about selected axes.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a gear mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IGearMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">IGearMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1.
3. Specify other properties of the GearMateFeatureData object.
To edit a gear mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a GearMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the GearMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete a gear mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.ActivateGroundPlane">IAssemblyDoc::ActivateGroundPlane</see> to activate the ground plane on the level where you want to insert a published asset; the asset's ground face snaps to the assembly's activated ground plane. Only one ground plane can be active at a given time in each assembly configuration.

Type.Description: Allows access to indicators and XML strings for symbols in a Gtol feature control frame.
Type.Remarks:
A geometric tolerance symbol adds geometric tolerances to parts and drawings using feature control frames.
This interface extends <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IGtol">IGtol</see> by supporting the new SOLIDWORKS 2022 Gtol architecture and providing the ability to specify Gtol frames using XML:
- Left of Gtol you can add a single line of text and symbol (first frame only).
- Above Gtol you can add multi-line text and symbol (top frame only).
- Right of Gtol there can be indicator, datum, or text box. Multiple indicators are supported, but any text box must be at the end of the list of indicators. Text box can have only one line and symbol.
- Below Gtol there can be additional frames, text, between instruction, from-to instruction, separate requirement label (bottom frame only).
For more information, see the **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Detailing and Drawings > Annotations > Symbols > Geometric Tolerance Symbols** topic.

Type.Name: IHingeMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a hinge mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A hinge mate:
- Limits the movement between two components to one rotational degree of freedom.
- Can also limit the angular movement between two components.
- Acts like a concentric mate and a coincident mate.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a hinge mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IHingeMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">IHingeMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> for each EntityType or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1 for the concentric entities, Mark = 32768 for the coincident entities, and Mark = 65536 for the angle entities.
3. Specify other properties of the HingeMateFeatureData object as required.
To edit a hinge mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a HingeMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the HingeMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete a hinge mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Name: IImport3DInterconnectData
Type.Description: Allows access to 3D Interconnect feature data.

Example.Name: Use 3D Interconnect to Import Third-Party Native CAD Files

Type.Remarks:
This interface requires 3D Interconnect. Enable 3D Interconnect by:
- Setting **Tools > Options > System Options > Import > Enable 3D Interconnect**.
- or -
- Calling <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.SetUserPreferenceToggle">ISldWorks::SetUserPreferenceToggle</see>(<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swUserPreferenceToggle_e">swUserPreferenceToggle_e</see>.swMultiCAD_Enable3DInterconnect, True).
Access this interface after importing a third-party native CAD file into:
- an existing SOLIDWORKS part using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.InsertImportedFeature">IPartDoc::InsertImportedFeature</see>.
- an existing SOLIDWORKS assembly using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.InsertImportedComponent">IAssemblyDoc::InsertImportedComponent</see>.
- a new SOLIDWORKS part using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.LoadFile4">ISldWorks::LoadFile4</see>.
- a new SOLIDWORKS assembly using ISldWorks::LoadFile4.
Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Is3DInterconnectFeature">IFeature::Is3DInterconnectFeature</see> to determine whether a feature is a 3D Interconnect feature and whether this interface applies.
ISldWorks::LoadFile4 imports into the appropriate native SOLIDWORKS part or assembly as follows:
- For both imported parts and assemblies, you can:
- Determine whether an update is required (<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Is3DInterconnectUpdateAvailable">IFeature::Is3DInterconnectUpdateAvailable</see>) and update the model (<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.Update3DInterconnectModel">IFeature::Update3DInterconnectModel</see>).
- Edit the imported data using this interface, its accessor (IFeature::GetImportedFeatureParameters), or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.SetImportedFeatureParameters">IFeature::SetImportedFeatureParameters</see>.
- Break the link to the original third-party native CAD file using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.BreakLink">IFeature::BreakLink</see>. After you break a link, all references to the original CAD file are lost, and you can no longer change the features to transfer from the original file.
- For imported parts only, the native SOLIDWORKS file created is a copy of the original non-native file. The copy retains an external reference to the original third-party native CAD file. If the original CAD file is modified in its orginal application, the SOLIDWORKS copy can be updated to import those changes. Changes to the SOLIDWORKS copy do not propagate back to the original CAD file.
- For imported assemblies only, after import you must save the new SOLIDWORKS assembly in order for SOLIDWORKS to import and create a copy to edit. Only after saving the new SOLIDWORKS assembly can you edit the imported top-level assembly or break its reference links. Editing lower-level imported components or individually breaking their reference links is not supported.
3D Interconnect supports the following third-party native CAD file formats and versions:
- ACIS: .sat, .sab, .asat, .asab for r1 - 2018 1.0
- Autodesk® Inventor: .ipt for V6-V2018, .iam for V11 - V2018
- CATIA® V5: .CATPart, .CATProduct for V5R8 - V5-6R2017
- IGES: .igs, .iges for up to 5.3
- JT: .jt for JT 8.x, 9.x, and 10.x
- PTC®: .prt, .prt.*, .asm.* for Pro/ENGINEER® 16 - Creo 4.0
- Solid Edge®: .par, .asm, .psm for V18 - ST10
- STEP: .stp, .step for AP203, AP214, AP242
- NX™ software: .prt for UG 11 - NX 11

Type.Name: IImportDxfDwgData
Type.Description: Allows you to specify values when importing or inserting DXF/DWG data.

Example.Name: Import DXF File into Part Sketch
Insert and Position DXF/DWG File in Drawing
Insert and Position DXF/DWG File in Drawing
Insert and Position DXF/DWG File in Drawing
Insert DXF/DWG File and Add Dimensions
Insert DXF/DWG File and Add Dimensions
Insert DXF/DWG File and Add Dimensions

Type.Remarks:
When importing DXF/DWG data, you can:
- Let SOLIDWORKS determine the default values:
- Paper size and sheet scale are computed to fit the input data.
- Length unit is determined from the header of the input DXF/DWG file.
- Sheet name is the same as the layout name in the input DXF/DWG file.
- or -
- Set your own values by using:
1. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.GetImportFileData">ISldWorks::GetImportFileData</see> to obtain the IImportDxfDwgData interface.
2. Use the following methods with a Sheet argument of "" (an empty string), to set up your defaults before importing or inserting the file:
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.GetPaperSize">IImportDxfDwgData::GetPaperSize</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.GetPosition">IImportDxfDwgData::GetPosition</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.GetSheetScale">IImportDxfDwgData::GetSheetScale</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.ImportMethod">IImportDxfDwgData::ImportMethod</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.LengthUnit">IImportDxfDwgData::LengthUnit</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.SetPaperSize">IImportDxfDwgData::SetPaperSize</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.SetPosition">IImportDxfDwgData::SetPosition</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.SetSheetScale">IImportDxfDwgData::SetSheetScale</see>
- <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IImportDxfDwgData.SheetName">IImportDxfDwgData::SheetName</see>
** NOTES:**
- Getting the IImportDxfDwgData interface does not get default values from the input file. Any values not set by you are set to the values computed by SOLIDWORKS.
- If the DWG/DXF file has multiple sheets, use these methods with a valid layout name in the Sheet argument to set up sheet specific settings, which override the default settings. If any of the individual items are not specified for a given layout name, the value used is from the defaults (layout name ""). If the default value is not specified, SOLIDWORKS computes and uses a meaningful value for that item.
When inserting DXF/DWG data as a feature into the current model document, first select a plane or planar surface and then call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertDwgOrDxfFile2">IFeatureManager::InsertDwgOrDxfFile2</see>.
Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.LoadFile4">ISldWorks::LoadFile4</see> to import the DXF/DWG file as a new SOLIDWORKS model document.

Type.Name: ILibraryFormToolFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to library forming tool feature data.
Type.Remarks:
To create a library forming tool feature:
1. Ensure that the Sheet Metal tab is visible on the CommandManager toolbar.
2. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByRay">IModelDocExtension::SelectByRay</see> to select a flat face (with Mark = 0) on which to use a forming tool.
3. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateDefinition">IFeatureManager::CreateDefinition</see>(swFmFormToolInstance) to create this feature data object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILibraryFormToolFeatureData.OverrideDocumentSettings">ILibraryFormToolFeatureData::OverrideDocumentSettings</see> to specify flat pattern visibility options.
5. Specify the forming tool and its rotation angle for placement using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILibraryFormToolFeatureData.FormToolConfiguration">ILibraryFormToolFeatureData::FormToolConfiguration</see>, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILibraryFormToolFeatureData.FormToolPath">FormToolPath</see>, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILibraryFormToolFeatureData.LinkToFormTool">LinkToFormTool</see>, and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILibraryFormToolFeatureData.RotationAngle">RotationAngle</see>.
6. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see> to create the feature.
To modify a library form tool feature:
1. Select a new location by clicking on a flat face in the graphics area where to re-position and/or replace the forming tool.
2. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to obtain this feature data object.
3. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILibraryFormToolFeatureData.AccessSelections">ILibraryFormToolFeatureData::AccessSelections</see>.
4. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILibraryFormToolFeatureData.SetPlacementFace">ILibraryFormToolFeatureData::SetPlacementFace</see> to re-position the forming tool.
5. Call ILibraryFormToolFeatureData::OverrideDocumentSettings to change the flat pattern visibility options.
6. Modify ILibraryFormToolFeatureData::FormToolConfiguration, FormToolPath (a change to FormToolPath changes the feature name), LinkToFormTool, and RotationAngle.
7. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> to finalize any changes or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILibraryFormToolFeatureData.ReleaseSelectionAccess">ILibraryFormToolFeatureData::ReleaseSelectionAccess</see> if no changes were made.
Forming tools are dies that dent, bend, stretch, or otherwise form sheet metal. For more information about forming tools, see the **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface online help > Sheet Metal > Using Forming Tools with Sheet Metal** topics.

Type.Name: ILinearCouplerMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to linear/linear coupler mate feature data.

Example.Name: Create and Edit Linear-Linear Coupler Mate
Create and Edit Linear-Linear Coupler Mate

Type.Remarks:
A linear/linear coupler mate establishes a relationship between the translation of one component and the translation of another component.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this advanced mate interface.
To create a linear/linear coupler mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILinearCouplerMateFeatureData.MateEntity1">ILinearCouplerMateFeatureData::MateEntity1</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILinearCouplerMateFeatureData.MateEntity2">ILinearCouplerMateFeatureData::MateEntity2</see>.
3. Specify other properties of the LinearCouplerMateFeatureData object as required.
To edit a linear/linear coupler mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a LinearCouplerMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the LinearCouplerMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete a linear/linear coupler mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Name: ILockMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to lock mate features.
Type.Remarks:
A lock mate:
- Maintains the position and orientation between two components.
- Fully constrains the components.
- Is like a rigid subasssembly of components.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a lock mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ILockMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">ILockMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities to mate using Mark = 1.
To edit a lock mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a LockMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the LockMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this lock mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Remarks:
SOLIDWORKS Model Based Definition (MBD) is an integrated drawingless manufacturing solution for SOLIDWORKS.
This interface and its methods and properties require that the SOLDWORKS MBD add-in be loaded. (<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.LoadAddIn">ISldWorks::LoadAddIn</see>)
The MBD3DPdfData object corresponds to the SOLIDWORKS MBD **Publish to 3D PDF** PropertyManager page.
Typical steps for generating a SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using the SOLIDWORKS API are:
1. Get the MBD3DPdfData object using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetMBD3DPdfData">IModelDocExtension::GetMBD3DPdfData</see>.
2. Set the path and file name of the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF theme using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.ThemeName">IMBD3DPdfData::ThemeName</see>.
3. Get standard and custom views using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.GetStandardViews">IMBD3DPdfData::GetStandardViews</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.GetMoreViews">IMBD3DPdfData::GetMoreViews</see>.
4. Set standard and custom views using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.SetStandardViews">IMBD3DPdfData::SetStandardViews</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.SetMoreViews">IMBD3DPdfData::SetMoreViews</see>.
5. Get and set text and custom properties in the theme using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.GetTextAndCustomProperties">IMBD3DPdfData::GetTextCustomProperties</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITextAndCustomProperty">ITextAndCustomProperty</see>.
6. Set the path for the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.FilePath">IMBD3DPdfData::FilePath</see>.
7. Generate the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.PublishTo3DPDF">IModelDocExtension::PublishTo3DPDF</see>.
See the SOLIDWORKS Help for details about MBD.

Type.Name: IMacroFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to the data that defines a macro feature.

Example.Name: Cut Body in Half Using Macro Feature

Type.Remarks:
**Macro features can...**
**For the** **rebuild function** **only, the macro associated with a macro feature cannot:**
- be inserted into a part, assembly, or drawing document
- create multiple bodies
- edit multiple existing bodies
- insert a feature from a macro feature in the same model
- edit definitions of other features if these features are in the same model as the macro feature
- rebuild, roll back, or roll forward the FeatureManager design tree
**NOTE:** These limitations are intended to prevent nested-feature regeneration in the model that contains the macro feature.
When the feature is creating multiple bodies, then the return value from the rebuild function should contain the array of bodies that are the result of the operation. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMacroFeatureData.EditBodies">IMacroFeatureData::EditBodies</see> is not expected to contain a body when the rebuild function returns to SOLIDWORKS.
When the feature is modifying a body and the result is multiple bodies, then IMacroFeatureData::EditBodies should contain all of the resulting bodies.
Whether creating multiple bodies or modifying a body that results in multiple bodies, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMacroFeatureData.EnableMultiBodyConsume">IMacroFeatureData::EnableMultiBodyConsume</see> from the <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Rebuild_Function.htm">rebuild</see> function to specify whether multiple bodies replace or append the original edit body in the FeatureManager design tree Solid Bodies folder.
If your application allows the user to decide which bodies to keep, your application must determine what it means to select the bodies and subsequently store the selected bodies with the feature.
To edit a macro feature in a drawing, do not use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMacroFeatureData.AccessSelections">IMacroFeatureData::AccessSelections</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMacroFeatureData.IAccessSelections">IMacroFeatureData::IAccessSelections</see>, or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IMacroFeatureData.ReleaseSelectionAccess">IMacroFeatureData::ReleaseSelectionAccess</see> because the concept of a rollback bar does not exist. You can still use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.IModifyDefinition2">IFeature::IModifyDefinition2</see> to update an IMacroFeatureData object.
If the user decides to cancel the changes made to the IMacroFeatureData object, then discard the IMacroFeatureData object. This action is equivalent to using IMacroFeatureData::ReleaseSelectionAccess.
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Macro_Features/Overview_of_Macro_Features.htm">Overview of Macro Features</see> for more information.

Type.Name: IMateControllerFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a mate controller feature.
Type.Remarks:
To create a mate controller feature:
- Use IAssemblyDoc::IsSupportedMatesAvailable to determine whether supportive mates exist for the assembly.
If true:
1. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CollectAllSupportiveMates">IAssemblyDoc::CollectAllSupportiveMates</see>.
2. Pre-select the supportive mates to use to create the mate controller. Or call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateControllerFeatureData.Initialize">IMateControllerFeatureData::Initialize</see>, passing in the supportive mates. Mates passed into the Initialize method are given precedence over pre-selected mates. The array passed in must contain IDispatch objects.
3. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateDefinition">IFeatureManager::CreateDefinition</see> to create an IMateControllerFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateControllerFeatureData.AddNewPosition">IMateControllerFeatureData::AddNewPosition</see> to add a new mate position to the mate controller.
5. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateControllerFeatureData.SetValues">IMateControllerFeatureData::SetValues</see> to set the values for all mates in a given mate position. If values are not specified or invalid values are specified, then the mate controller feature is created with default mate values (i.e., values used when the mate was created).
6. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see>, passing in the IMateControllerFeatureData object.
7. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.GetCreateFeatureErrors">IFeatureManager::GetCreateFeatureErrors</see>.
To edit a mate controller feature, call:
1. <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see>
2. <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateControllerFeatureData.AccessSelections">IMateControllerFeatureData::AccessSelections</see>
3. <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>
4. <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateControllerFeatureData.ReleaseSelectionAccess">IMateControllerFeatureData::ReleaseSelectionAccess</see>
For more information about the Mate Controller feature, see the **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Assemblies > Mates > Mate Controller** topic.

Type.Name: IMathTransform
Type.Description: Provides a simplified interface for manipulating transformation matrix data.

Example.Name: Get Patterned Cosmetic Thread Annotations Data
Get Patterned Cosmetic Thread Annotations Data
Get Patterned Cosmetic Thread Annotations Data

Type.Remarks:
Transformation matrix data:
|a b c . n |
|d e f . o |
|g h i . p |
|j k l . m |
The SOLIDWORKS transformation matrix is stored as a homogeneous matrix of 16 elements, ordered as shown. The first 9 elements (a to i) are elements of a 3x3 rotational sub-matrix, the next 3 elements (j,k,l) define a translation vector, and the next 1 element (m) is a scaling factor. The last 3 elements (n,o,p) are unused in this context.
The 3x3 rotational sub-matrix represents 3 axis sets:
- row 1 for x-axis components of rotation
- row 2 for y-axis components of rotation
- row 3 for z-axis components of rotation
The 3 axes are constrained to be orthogonal and unified so that they produce a pure rotational transformation. Reflections can also be added to these axes by setting the components to negative. The rotation sub-matrix coupled with the lower-left translation vector and the lower-right corner scaling factor creates an affine transformation, which is a transformation that preserves lines and parallelism; i.e., maps parallel lines to parallel lines.
If the 3 axis sets of the 3x3 rotational sub-matrix are not orthogonal or unified, then they are automatically corrected according to the following rules:
- If any axis is 0, or any two axes are parallel, or all axes are coplanar, then an identity matrix replaces the rotational sub-matrix.
- All axes are corrected to be of unit length.
- The axes are built to be orthogonal to each other in the prioritized order of Z, X, Y (X is orthogonal to Z, Y is orthogonal to Z and X).

Type.Name: IModelDoc2
Type.Description: Allows access to SOLIDWORKS documents: parts, assemblies, and drawings.

Example.Name: Get Names of Creators of Features

Type.Remarks:
There are three main SOLIDWORKS document types:
- parts
- assemblies
- drawings
Each document type has its own object (<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc">IPartDoc</see>, <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc">IAssemblyDoc</see>, and <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc">IDrawingDoc</see>) with its own set of related functions. For example, the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.AddComponent4">IAssemblyDoc::AddComponent4</see> method exists on the IAssemblyDoc object because adding components is specific to assembly documents.
The SOLIDWORKS API also has functions that are common to all document types. For example, printing, saving, or determining the file name associated with a document would be common operations. To expose common document-level functions, the SOLIDWORKS API uses the IModelDoc2 object.

Type.Name: IMotionPlotAxisFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a plot's x- and y-axis feature data.
Type.Remarks:
Typical steps for creating a motion study's plot data and plot:
1. Open an assembly model and create the motion study.
2. Select the model's entities whose motion you want to measure.
3. Perform the calculations and get the results.
4. Create a plot feature data.
5. Create the plot's x-axis and y-axis feature data objects.
6. Set the type of plot.
7. Select the result component.
8. Set the entities for the x-axis and y-axis feature data objects.
9. Get the plot's x-axis and y-axis values and insert and display the plot.
Examine the examples to see the calls for these steps.

Type.Name: IParallelMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a parallel mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A parallel mate places selected items a constant distance apart.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a parallel mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IParallelMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">IParallelMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities to mate using Mark = 1.
3. Specify other properties of the ParallelMateFeatureData object.
To edit a parallel mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a ParallelMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the ParallelMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this parallel mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Name: IPartExplodeStep
Type.Description: Allows access to the explode step of an explode view of a multibody part.
Type.Remarks:
This interface is valid only for an active current explode view of a multibody part. To create an explode view of a multibody part, call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.CreateExplodedView">IPartDoc::CreateExplodedView</see>.
The setter properties and methods of this interface:
- Always clear selection lists.
- Do not work if the Explode PropertyManager is open.
- Do not work if any body is being edited in the context of the multibody part.
To edit an explode step:
1. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.ShowExploded">IPartDoc::ShowExploded</see> to activate the explode view of interest.
2. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPartDoc.GetExplodedViewConfigurationName">IPartDoc::GetExplodedViewConfigurationName</see> to get the configuration for the explode view.
3. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IConfiguration.GetPartExplodeStep">IConfiguration::GetPartExplodeStep</see> to access the explode step of interest.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select:
1. Bodies to move with Mark = 1.
2. An explode direction entity (cylindrical <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFace2">face</see>, conical face, linear <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEdge">edge</see>, or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRefAxis">axis</see>) with Mark = 2.
5. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObject6">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObject6</see> to get the bodies selected in step 4a.
6. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPartExplodeStep.SetBodies">IPartExplodeStep::SetBodies</see>, passing in the bodies gotten in step 4a.
7. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPartExplodeStep.SetExplodeDirection">IPartExplodeStep::SetExplodeDirection</see>, passing in the explode direction entity that was selected in step 4b. See **Notes**.
8. Modify other explode step properties.
**Notes**:
When editing the object entity for the explode direction, please bear in mind:
If... Then...
Both object and manipulator index are valid Both object and manipulator index are set.
Manipulator index is valid, but object is invalid Manipulator index is set, and object is unchanged.
Object is valid, but manipulator index is invalid
Object is set, and the manipulator index is reset to the Z direction index.
Both object and manipulator index are invalid No values change.
For more information, see **Exploded Views in Multibody Parts** topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.
To access explode steps of explode views of assemblies, see <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IExplodeStep">IExplodeStep</see>.

Example.Name: Create and Edit Profile Center Mate
Create and Edit Profile Center Mate

Type.Remarks:
A profile center mate centrally aligns rectangular and circular profiles to each other and fully defines the components.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this advanced mate interface.
To create a profile center mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IProfileCenterMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">IProfileCenterMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1.
3. Specify other properties of the ProfileCenterMateFeatureData object.
To edit a profile center mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a ProfileCenterMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the ProfileCenterMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete a profile center mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Remarks:
To create a projection curve feature:
1. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the necessary entities using the following Marks:
- target faces on which to project a sketch = 1
- sketch to project = 2
- target sketch on which to project a sketch = 4
- projection direction entity = 8
2. Call IFeatureManager::CreateDefinition(swFmRefCurve) to access this interface.
3. Set non-entity properties on this interface.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see> to create the projection curve feature.
See the SOLIDWORKS Help for more information about projection curve features.

Type.Name: IPropertyManagerPage2
Type.Description: Provides add-in applications the ability to display and use views that have the look and feel of SOLIDWORKS PropertyManager pages.
Type.Remarks:
OK and Cancel buttons are optional for IPropertyManagerPage2 objects, but a Help button is always displayed. If you do not want to implement help for your add-in, return false on help notification to display SOLIDWORKS Help.
PropertyManager controls are displayed in a single, left-aligned column. Slight vertical spacing adjustment is available with the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPropertyManagerPageGroup.AddControl">IPropertyManagerPageGroup::AddControl</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPropertyManagerPageGroup.IAddControl">IPropertyManagerPageGroup::IAddControl</see> or the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPropertyManagerPage2.AddControl">PropertyManagerPage2::AddControl</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPropertyManagerPage2.IAddControl">IPropertyManagerPage2::IAddControl</see> Options argument.
Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetUserPreferenceInteger">IModelDocExtension::GetUserPreferenceInteger</see>(swPropertyManagerColorDivider,UserPrefOption) to get the color of the PropertyManager divider box backgrounds for custom bitmap color blending purposes. The returned integer value is the COLORREF value.
The add-in application must implement the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swpublished.IPropertyManagerPage2Handler8">IPropertyManagerPage2Handler8</see> interface for data to be exchanged with the add-in application. The add-in application owns the IPropertyManagerPage2 object, which owns the IPropertyManagerPage2Handler8 for that page.
The limits on the number of controls on a PropertyManager page are:
- Total number of controls = 300 (This number does not include group and selection boxes.)
- Total number of group boxes = 20
- Total number of selection boxes = 15
**NOTE**: Number boxes count as 2 controls. All other controls count as 1 control.
SOLIDWORKS does not allow suppressing components or features while a PropertyManager page is open.
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/overview/Using_PropertyManagerPage2_and_the_Related_Objects.htm">Using PropertyManagerPage2 and the Related Objects</see> for more information.

Type.Name: IPropertyManagerPage2Handler9
Type.Description: Must be implemented by the add-in application to handle callbacks from <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPropertyManagerPage2">IPropertyManagerPage2</see>.
Type.Remarks:
To use this interface:
- In a SOLIDWORKS VBA macro, you must reference the **SOLIDWORKS exposed type libraries for add-in use** type library specific to the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks.VersionHistory">version of SOLIDWORKS</see> that you are running.
- In a SOLIDWORKS VB.NET or C# add-in, you must reference the **SOLIDWORKS.interop.swpublished** assembly and set ComVisibleAttribute to true (see <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/ComVisibleAttribute_in_VSTA_macros.htm">ComVisibleAttribute in VB.NET or C# Macros and Add-ins</see>).
For all unimplemented methods of this object, the add-in application can return E_NOTIMPL.

Type.Name: IPropertyManagerPageButton
Type.Description: Allows you to access a <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPropertyManagerPage2">PropertyManager page</see> button control.
Type.Remarks:
Users can resize PropertyManager pages horizontally in SOLIDWORKS 2006 and later. This change in functionality affects the appearance of the buttons on PropertyManager pages created in SOLIDWORKS 2005 and earlier.
In SOLIDWORKS 2005 and earlier, buttons remained aligned vertically at an indented position when a user resized a PropertyManager page. In most instances, these buttons are now centered when a user resizes a PropertyManager page. However, if a button on a PropertyManager page was aligned at the very left edge of the page and it was the only button on that line, then it is assumed that it was intentionally placed at that position and it will stay at that position if a user resizes the page. Any text on the button will also be left justified inside the button. If a button has a bitmap as its label, then the button remains next to the label instead of being centered.
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/overview/Using_PropertyManagerPage2_and_the_Related_Objects.htm">Using PropertyManagerPage2 and the Related Objects</see> for more information.
