Type.Remarks:
If you implement a...
Then...
Spin box
an edit box with attached up and down arrow buttons for incrementing and decrementing the value is created.
Combo box/spin box
a text box with:
- a down-arrow button to display the attached drop-down list. You must set up and control the attached drop-down list
- up and down buttons for incrementing and decrementing the value
is created.
Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPropertyManagerPageNumberbox.Style">IPropertyManagerPageNumberbox::Style</see> to select the type of combo-box/spin-box number box you want to implement.
For both types of number boxes, SOLIDWORKS automatically validates the values and units. The up and down arrow buttons automatically increment and decrement the value. Both types of number boxes:
- Accept numerical expressions.
- Store all values as meters or radians and display them in the units specified in the current unit settings.
**NOTE:** When a document's unit system is set to a non-metric setting, the dimension precision value (the number of digits displayed after a decimal point) is based on the number of digits specified. It is not based on the document's dimension precision settings.

Type.Name: IPunchTable
Type.Description: Allows access to punch table information and values.
Type.Remarks:
Punch tables contain information about the punches that are created by forming tools in sheet metal parts. A punch table contains the following information about pre-selected punches:
Column Description
TAG Datum tag added to each punch in the flat pattern view
PUNCH ID Property of the forming tool or library feature
X Location Distance from the x-axis to the point of insertion of the forming tool in the flat pattern view
Y Location Distance from the y-axis to the point of insertion of the forming tool in the flat pattern view
ANGLE Angle between the x-axis and the forming tool
QUANTITY Number of times that the forming tool is used in the flat pattern view

Type.Remarks: The IPunchTableAnnotation object is derived from the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITableAnnotation">ITableAnnotation</see> object.

Type.Name: IRackPinionMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a rack and pinion mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A rack and pinion mate consists of two components where:
- One component (the rack) causes circular rotation in another component (the pinion) and vice versa.
- Neither component is required to have gear teeth.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a rack and pinion mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 64 for the rack edge and Mark = 128 for the pinion face.
3. Specify other properties of the RackPinionMateFeatureData object as required.
To edit a rack and pinion mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a RackPinionMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the RackPinionMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this rack and pinion mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Name: IRefPlaneFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to reference plane feature data.
Type.Remarks:
Before calling any of the methods and properties on this interface, you should determine the reference plane's type because some IRefPlaneFeatureData methods and properties only work with constraint-based reference planes and some only work with non-constrained reference planes. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRefPlaneFeatureData.Type2">IRefPlaneFeatureData::Type2</see> to determine the type of reference plane.
If IRefPlaneFeatureData::Type2 returns swRefPlaneConstraintBase, then the reference plane is constraint based. To determine if a constraint-based reference plane has angle or offset distances references, call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRefPlaneFeatureData.Type">IRefPlaneFeatureData::Type</see>:
- swRefPlaneAngle is returned for angle references.
- swRefPlaneDistance is returned for offset distance references.
Otherwise, the reference plane is not constraint based. Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRefPlaneFeatureData.Type">IRefPlaneFeatureData::Type</see> to determine its type.
**NOTE:** Reference planes created in SOLIDWORKS 2010 or later are constraint based; reference planes created in SOLIDWORKS 2009 or earlier are not.

Type.Name: IRenamedDocumentReferences
Type.Description: Allows you to update references to a renamed file in unopened documents.
Type.Remarks:
This interface corresponds to the Rename Documents dialog box in the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface.
To update references to a renamed file in unopened documents:
1. Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.UpdateWhereUsedReferences">IRenamedDocumentReferences::UpdateWhereUsedReferences</see> to true.
2. Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.IncludeFileLocations">IRenamedDocumentReferences::IncludeFileLocations</see> to true to search the folders listed under **Referenced Documents** in **Tools > Options > System Options > File Locations.**
3. Add or remove folders in which to search using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.AddSearchFolder">IRenamedDocumentReferences::AddSearchFolder</see> or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.RemoveSearchFolder">IRenamedDocumentReferences::RemoveSearchFolder</see>, respectively.
4. Get the folders to search using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.GetSearchPath">IRenamedDocumentReferences::GetSearchPath</see>.
5. Search for references using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.Search">IRenamedDocumentReferences::Search</see>.
6. Get the references found in the previous step using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.ReferencesArray">IRenamedDocumentReferences::ReferenceArray</see>.
7. Remove a reference from the update using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.RemoveReference">IRenamedDocumentReferences::RemoveReference</see>.
8. Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IRenamedDocumentReferences.CompletionAction">IRenamedDocumentReferences::CompletionAction</see> to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swRenamedDocumentFinalAction_e">swRenamedDocumentFinalAction_e</see>.swRenamedDocumentFinalAction_Ok.

Type.Name: IRevisionCloud
Type.Description: Allows access to a revision cloud annotation.

Example.Name: Insert Revision Cloud into a Drawing
Insert Revision Cloud into a Drawing
Insert Revision Cloud into a Drawing

Type.Remarks:
To create a revision cloud in a drawing document, call:
1. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.InsertRevisionCloud">IDrawingDoc::InsertRevisionCloud</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc.IInsertRevisionCloud">IDrawingDoc::IInsertRevisionCloud</see>.
2. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRevisionCloud.GetAnnotation">IRevisionCloud::GetAnnotation</see> or <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRevisionCloud.IGetAnnotation">IRevisionCloud::IGetAnnotation</see> to get the annotation object for the revision cloud.
3. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IAnnotation.SetPosition">IAnnotation::SetPosition</see> to set the revision cloud position point on the drawing. If you eliminate this step, the revision cloud is rendered starting at the drawing origin of x=0, y=0, z=0. Set the revision cloud position point as follows:
For revision cloud shape... Set the revision cloud position point to...
Ellipse The center of the revision cloud.
Rectangle A corner of the revision cloud.
Polygon One of the points on the revision cloud.
Freehand One of the points on the revision cloud.
4. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRevisionCloud.ArcRadius">IRevisionCloud::ArcRadius</see> to set the arc radius of the revision cloud.
5. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRevisionCloud.SetPathPointAtIndex">IRevisionCloud::SetPathPointAtIndex</see> one or more times with Index = -1 to create points on the revision cloud as follows:
For revision cloud shape... Call IRevisionCloud::SetPathPointAtIndex...
Ellipse Once, specifying the coordinates of a corner of the ellipse-inscribed rectangle.
Rectangle Once, specifying the coordinates of a corner opposite the revision cloud position point.
Polygon (Number of polygon sides + 1) times, such that the first and last points coincide with the revision cloud position point.
Freehand Indefinite number of times, such that the first and last points coincide with the revision cloud position point.
6. <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IRevisionCloud.Finalize">IRevisionCloud::Finalize</see> to close the revision cloud path. Once the revision cloud path is closed, you can no longer add points to it.
7. IRevisionCloud::SetPathPointAtIndex to modify the position of an existing point on the revision cloud.

Type.Name: ISMGussetFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a sheet metal gusset feature.
Type.Remarks:
To create a sheet metal gusset feature:
1. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateDefinition">IFeatureManager::CreateDefinition</see> to instantiate this feature data object.
2. Pre-select faces, lines, edges, vertices, or points as follows:
To... Call <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to select...
Specify the legs of the gusset feature
- Two flat faces of a bend.
- or -
- Two flat faces adjacent to a cylindrical bend face.
- or -
- One cylindrical bend face.
- or -
- One flat face and one non-planar face adjacent to a toroidal bend.
- or -
- One toroidal bend face.
Optionally orient the gusset section plane
One linear edge or sketch segment that is perpendicular to the gusset section plane.
If you do not pre-select either entity, then the bend line adjacent to the gusset legs is used as the reference.
Optionally position the gusset section plane
One vertex, sketch point, or reference point.
If you do not pre-select any of these entities, then you must set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMGussetFeatureData.UseOffset">ISMGussetFeatureData::UseOffset</see> to true and specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMGussetFeatureData.OffsetDistance">ISMGussetFeatureData::OffsetDistance</see> to define the reference point. For insertion of the first gusset, the assumed reference point is on the end of the sheet metal bend. For second and subsequent gusset insertions, the assumed reference point is on the edge of the gusset last inserted.
3. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMGussetFeatureData.ProfileDimensionScheme">ISMGussetFeatureData::ProfileDimensionScheme</see> and modify other properties on this feature data object as follows:
If ISMGussetFeatureData::ProfileDimensionScheme=
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swSheetMetalGussetProfileDimType_e">swSheetMetalGussetProfileDimType_e</see>.
swSheetMetalGussetProfileDimType_ProfileDimensions, to dimension the gusset profile using...
Specify ISMGussetFeatureData::...
Both legs of the gusset
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMGussetFeatureData.ProfileLengthDim">ProfileLengthDim</see> for d1 leg
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMGussetFeatureData.ProfileHeightDim">ProfileHeightDim</see> for d2 leg
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMGussetFeatureData.UseAngleDimForProfile">UseAngleDimForProfile</see> = false
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMGussetFeatureData.FlipDimSides">FlipDimSides</see> = true to swap d1 and d2 legs during dimensioning
d1 leg and the angle it forms with the gusset
- ProfileLengthDim for d1 leg
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMGussetFeatureData.ProfileAngleDim">ProfileAngleDim</see> of angle formed by gusset intersecting d1 leg
- UseAngleDimForProfile = true
- FlipDimSides = true to swap d1 and d2 legs during dimensioning
d2 leg and the angle it forms with the gusset
- ProfileHeightDim for d2 leg
- ProfileAngleDim of angle formed by gusset intersecting d2 leg
- UseAngleDimForProfile = true
- FlipDimSides = true to swap d1 and d2 legs during dimensioning
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see>.

Type.Name: ISMNormalCutFeatureData2
Type.Description: Allows access to a sheet metal normal cut feature.
Type.Remarks:
Extruded cuts that pierce models at an angle have non-normal side walls. To make these side walls normal, you create a normal cut feature.
To create a normal cut feature:
1. Open a sheet metal part that has a cut-extrude with non-normal side walls.
2. Call IFeatureManager::CreateDefinition(swFmNormalCut) to access this interface.
3. Set non-entity properties on this interface.
4. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByRay">IModelDocExtension::SelectByRay</see> or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> with Mark = 4 to select the offset plane, only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.NormalCutParameters">ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::NormalCutParameters</see> is set to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.swNormalCutParameters_e">swNormalCutParameters_e</see>.swNormalCutOffsetPlane.
5. Use IModelDocExtension::SelectByRay or IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 with Mark = 8 to select the direction of the normal cut, only if ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::NormalCutParameters is set to swNormalCutParameters_e.swNormalCutExtent.
6. Use IModelDocExtension::SelectByRay or IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 with Mark = 1 to select each non-normal face in the group. If <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.AutoPropagation">ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::AutoPropagation</see> is set to true, then all faces tangent to a selected face are automatically added to the face group.
7. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.CreateGroup">ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::CreateGroup</see> to access <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutGroupData">ISMNormalCutGroupData</see>.
8. Repeat steps 6 and 7 as many times as you have face groups. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDoc2.ClearSelection2">IModelDoc2::ClearSelection2</see> after each face group is created.
9. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see>.
To edit a normal cut feature:
1. Call IFeature::GetDefinition to get this feature data object for a selected normal cut feature.
2. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.AccessSelections">ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::AccessSelections</see>. **Note:** **Any selections made **before** this call are invalid. To edit the properties of this feature, you must re-select their entities during the editing session, i.e., after calling ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::AccessSelections. (See step 5.)**
3. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.GetGroupNames">ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::GetGroupNames</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.GetGroupByName">ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::GetGroupByName</see> to access ISMNormalCutGroupData for an existing face group.
4. Call ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::CreateGroup to create another face group if needed.
5. Modify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.CutDirection">cut direction</see>, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.OffsetPlaneReference">offset plane reference</see>, or other properties on ISMNormalCutFeatureData2 as needed. To select property entities, use IModelDocExtension::SelectByRay or IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 followed by <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObject6">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObject6</see>. You can also use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IEntity.Select4">IEntity::Select4</see>.
6. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see> if you modifed the feature or <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISMNormalCutFeatureData2.ReleaseSelectionAccess">ISMNormalCutFeatureData2::ReleaseSelectionAccess</see> if you did not.

Type.Name: ISWPropertySheet
Type.Description: Allows applications to add pages to certain property sheets that are exported by the SOLIDWORKS Design application.
Type.Remarks:
See <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.swconst.swPropSheetType_e">swPropSheetType_e</see> for a list of the property sheets that support this functionality.
An example of a property sheet is the dialog that is displayed when you click **Tools >** **Options**. This dialog consists of a base property sheet and property pages stacked on top of it. To display a specific property page, click its tab.
The MFC class that implements a property sheet is CPropertysheet, and the MFC class that implements a property page is CPropertyPage. ISWPropertySheet is a OLE wrapper class over the SOLIDWORKS CPropertysheet class. This means that SOLIDWORKS API programmers can add their own CPropertyPages to a SOLIDWORKS Design property sheet.
A SOLIDWORKS Design property sheet is different from an <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IPropertyManagerPage2">IPropertyManager</see> page. A PropertyManager page is displayed when the PropertyManager tab is selected on the left-side panel. PropertyManager pages have replaced numerous dialogs.
**Creating PropertyPages**
When a property sheet is created that can have pages added to it, the notification swAppPropertySheetCreateNotify is sent via the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks">ISldWorks</see> interface. This notification is sent as swAppPropertySheetCreateNotify( LPDISPATCH sheet, long type) where sheet is the IDispatch interface of a ISWPropertySheet object and type is an enumerated constant of type swPropSheetType_e.
When the application receives this notification, it can check the type of the sheet from the type argument. If pages are to be added, then the sequence of operations is:
- Ensure that the application resources will be used to make the page (for example by calling AfxSetResourceHandle())
- Create the CPropertyPage-derived class
- For 32-bit applications, pass the CPropertyPage object to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISWPropertySheet.AddPage">ISWPropertySheet::AddPage</see>, casting the CPropertyPage* to a long
- For 64-bit applications, pass the CPropertyPage object to <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISWPropertySheet.AddPagex64">ISWPropertySheet::AddPagex64</see>, casting the CPropertyPage* to a long long
- Reset the resources to their previous state
**Destroying PropertyPages**
The CPropertyPage PostNcDestroy function is called by the SOLIDWORKS Design application when the property sheet is being destroyed. At this point, the application should delete any objects (for example the CPropertyPage object.)
Events are implemented with delegates in the Microsoft .NET Framework. See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks_namespace">Overview</see> topic for a list of delegates for this interface.

Type.Name: ISafeArrayUtility
Type.Description:
Access the ISafeArrayUtility interface, which can:
- get an unpacked array of native SOLIDWORKS Dispatch-based objects of the same data type and return a packed Variant SafeArray to use in methods that requires passing a packed Variant SafeArray.
- get a packed Variant SafeArray and return an unpacked array of native SOLIDWORKS Dispatch-based objects of the same data type.
- get a Variant SafeArray and return the number of SafeArray objects in the Variant SafeArray and their data type.
- get and put a value in a Variant SafeArray of the same data type.

Example.Name: Get Scale Factor of Each Model View

Type.Remarks:
The ISafeArrayUtility interface replaces the SOLIDWORKS SafeArray template class, which you might have used in earlier versions of SOLIDWORKS to instantiate SafeArrays for methods requiring Variant arrays in your C++ projects.
This ISafeArrayUtility interface's methods are only compatible with raw pointers and BSTRs; this interface's methods are not compatible with smart pointers (i.e., reference counted) or the Active Template Library (ATL) class CComBSTR. For example:
IDispatch* pDisp1; //This works IDispatchPtr pDisp2 //This does not work CComPtr pDisp3 //This does not work
BSTR fileName1 //This works CComBSTR fileName2 //This does not work

Type.Name: IScrewMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a screw mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A screw mate consists of two components, where:
- Components are concentric.
- Translation of one component along the axis causes rotation of the other component according to a pitch relationship.
- Rotation of one component causes translation of the other component.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a screw mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IScrewMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">IScrewMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1.
3. Specify other properties of the ScrewMateFeatureData object. as required.
To edit a screw mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a ScrewMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the ScrewMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this screw mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

A simple corner is the position in a structure system where the ends of two members meet either in a body trim or a planar trim fashion.
In the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface, the Simple Corner PropertyManager contains two lists that you can manage using the APIs in this interface and elsewhere:

(Optional) For both fillets and chamfers, set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.KeepFeatures">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::KeepFeatures</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.PropagateToTangentFaces">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::PropagateToTangentFaces</see>.
4. (Optional) For fillets only, set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.RoundCorners">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::RoundCorners</see>, <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.ConstantWidth">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConstantWidth</see>, and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.CurvatureContinuous">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::CurvatureContinuous</see> (if set to true, then ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::RoundCorners and ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConicTypeForCrossSectionProfile are not valid).
5. If a **symmetric fillet/chamfer**: - For fillets or chamfers, set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.DefaultDistance">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultRadius</see> to a default fillet radius or chamfer offset distance. - For fillets, if ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::CurvatureContinuous is false and ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConicTypeForCrossSectionProfile is set to swFeatureFilletCircular, then you can set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.IsMultipleRadius">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::IsMultipleRadius</see>. If MultipleRadius is set to true, then you can call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.SetRadius">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::SetRadius</see> to specify multiple edge radii. If ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::CurvatureContinuous is false and ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConicTypeForCrossSectionProfile is set to swFeatureFilletConicRho or swFeatureFilletConicRadius, set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.DefaultConicRhoOrRadius">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultConicRhoOrRadius</see> to a conic rho value between 0.05 and 0.95, inclusive, or a conic radius value, respectively. - For chamfers, if ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::IsMultipleRadius is set to true, then you can call ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::SetRadius to set multiple offset distances.
6. If an **asymmetric fillet/chamfer**: - Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.AsymmetricFillet">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::AsymmetricFillet</see>.
- Set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultRadius to the fillet Distance 1 radius or chamfer Offset Distance 1. - Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.DefaultDistance">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultDistance</see> to the fillet Distance 2 radius or chamfer Offset Distance 2. - For fillets only, if ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::CurvatureContinuous is false and ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConicTypeForCrossSectionProfile is set to swFeatureFilletConicRho, set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultConicRhoOrRadius to a conic rho value between 0.05 and 0.95, inclusive.
For more information, see the **Constant Size Fillets** and **Chamfer PropertyManager** topics in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.
Face fillet/face-face chamfer
1. Call IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 with:
- Mark = 2 to select Face Set 1. - Mark = 4 to select Face Set 2.
1. (Optional) For both fillets and chamfers, set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::PropagateToTangentFaces and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.HelpPoint">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::HelpPoint</see>.
2. (Optional) For fillets only, set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::CurvatureContinuous (if set to true, then ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConicTypeForCrossSectionProfile is not valid).
3. If a **symmetric fillet/chamfer**: - Set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultRadius for the fillet radius or the chamfer offset distance. - For fillets only, if ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::CurvatureContinuous is false and ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConicTypeForCrossSectionProfile is set to swFeatureFilletConicRho or swFeatureFilletConicRadius, set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultConicRhoOrRadius to a conic rho or conic radius value.
4. If a **chord width fillet/chamfer**: - Set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultRadius to set the chord width. - For fillets only, if ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::CurvatureContinuous is false and ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConicTypeForCrossSectionProfile is set to swFeatureFilletConicRho or swFeatureFilletConicRadius, set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultConicRhoOrRadius to a conic rho or conic radius value.
5. If an **asymmetric fillet/chamfer**: - Set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::AsymmetricFillet. - Set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultRadius to the fillet Distance 1 radius or the chamfer Offset Distance 1. - Set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultDistance to the fillet Distance 2 radius or the chamfer Offset Distance 2. - For fillets only, if ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::CurvatureContinuous is false and ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::ConicTypeForCrossSectionProfile is set to swFeatureFilletConicRho, set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::DefaultConicRhoOrRadius to a conic rho value.
6. If a **hold line fillet/chamfer**: - Call IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 with Mark = 8 to select the hold line edges. - Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.HoldLines">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::HoldLines</see> to the hold line edges.
For more information, see the **Face Fillets** and **Chamfer PropertyManager** topics in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.
Full round fillet
1. Call IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 with: - Mark = 2 to select Face Set 1. - Mark = 512 to select Center Face Set. - Mark = 4 to select Face Set 2.
2. (Optional) Set ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::PropagateToTangentFaces.
For more information, see the **Full Round Fillets** topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.
Setback fillet
1. Follow the instructions above to create a constant radius fillet.
2. Use the setback methods on ISimpleFilletFeatureData2 to set the setback distances from setback vertices of fillet corners.
For more information, see the **Constant Size Fillets** topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.
Partial edge fillet/chamfer
1. Follow the instructions above to create a constant radius fillet or offset face chamfer.
2. Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.EnablePartialEdgeParameters">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::EnablePartialEdgeParameters</see> to true.
3. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.GetPartialEdgeFilletData">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::GetPartialEdgeFilletData</see>.
4. Set other properties of IPartialEdgeFilletData as required.
5. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleFilletFeatureData2.SetPartialEdgeFilletData">ISimpleFilletFeatureData2::SetPartialEdgeFilletData</see>, passing in the IPartialEdgeFilletData populated in step d.
6. Repeat steps c-e for each edge to partially fillet.
For more information, see the **Constant Size Fillets** and **Chamfer PropertyManager** topics in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.
5. Create the fillet/chamfer feature by calling <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.CreateFeature">IFeatureManager::CreateFeature</see>.
For more information about fillets, see the **Fillets** topic in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Miscellaneous/Accessing_Selections_that_Define_Features.htm">Accessing Selections that Define Features</see> for additional details.

Type.Name: ISldWorks
Type.Description: Provides direct and indirect access to all other interfaces exposed in the SOLIDWORKS API.

Example.Name: Get Names of Creators of Features

Type.Remarks:
This interface is the highest-level object in the SOLIDWORKS API. This interface provides a general set of functions that allow application-level operations such as create, open, close, and quit documents, arrange icons and windows, change the active document, and create attribute definitions.
Use CreateObject, GetObject, New, or similar functions to obtain the ISldWorks object from a Dispatch application (Visual Basic or C++ Dispatch). Standalone .exe C++ COM applications can use CoCreateInstance. All of the SOLIDWORKS API add-in wizards automatically create the ISldWorks object for you.
Events are implemented with delegates in the Microsoft .NET Framework. See the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks_namespace">Overview</see> topic for a list of delegates for this interface.

Type.Name: ISlicingData
Type.Description: Allows access to slicing tool data.
Type.Remarks:
You must pre-select the first slicing plane before you can access the default bounding box directions for slicing.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeatureManager.InsertSlicing">IFeatureManager::InsertSlicing</see> takes this data object and invokes the Slicing tool. The Slicing tool creates a parallel or radial series of slicing planes with sketches that intersect, or slice, the model.
For more information, see the **Slicing Tool** topics in the SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help.

Type.Name: ISlotMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a slot mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A slot mate is a mate between:
- A bolt and either a straight slot or an arced slot.
- Two slots, straight or arced
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a slot mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISlotMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">ISlotMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1.
3. Specify other properties of the SlotMateFeatureData object. as required.
To edit a slot mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a SlotMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the SlotMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this slot mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Name: ISmartComponentFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a Smart Component.
Type.Remarks:
A Smart Component is defined by:
- Components
- Features
- Feature references
A Smart Component is created in a training assembly. When the Smart Component is saved, it is saved with the training assembly in a SOLIDWORKS part.
When the Smart Component is inserted or edited in a target assembly, the training assembly opens in a small preview window, and the PropertyManager page of the Smart Component displays.
See the SOLIDWORKS Help for more information about Smart Components.
Use... To...
This interface
- Gain access to the training assembly of a Smart Component.
- Gain access to the selection lists on the PropertyManager page of a Smart Component.
- Insert features and components into a Smart Component.
- Delete features and components from a Smart Component.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.GetSmartComponentData">IComponent2::GetSmartComponentData</see> Get the current features, components, and feature references of a Smart Component.
<see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IComponent2.SetSmartComponentData">IComponent2::SetSmartComponentData</see> Change which features and components to enable in a Smart Component and to insert Smart Features in a target assembly.

Type.Name: IStructureSystemFolder
Type.Description: Allows access to a structure system folder.
Type.Remarks:
This interface accesses the top-level folder of a structure system in the FeatureManager design tree. The structure system folder contains one or more profile group folders. Each profile group folder contains profile references and structure system members.
When a structure system is created in the user interface, the Corner Management PropertyManager opens automatically. When structure systems are created using the API, a Corner Management*X* folder is automatically created for each structure system in the FeatureManager design tree.
A structure system and its corner management folder appears similar to the following in the FeatureManager design tree. In parentheses are the APIs that you use to access the corresponding item:
- **Structure System1** (IStructureSystemFolder accessors)
- **Structure System Grid1**
- **<3 x 5> (1)** (<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IProfileGroupFolder">IProfileGroupFolder</see> accessors)
- **Plane2** (profile reference plane - <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IProfileGroupFolder.GetPlane">IProfileGroupFolder::GetPlane</see>)
- **Sketch11** (profile sketch - <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IProfileGroupFolder.GetSketch">IProfileGroupFolder::GetSketch</see>)
- **Member1** (structure system member - <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IProfileGroupFolder.GetStructureSystemMembers">IProfileGroupFolder::GetStructureSystemMembers</see>)
- **Corner Management1** (<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerManagementFolder">ICornerManagementFolder</see> accessors)
- **Complex Corner Group1** (<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerTreatmentGroupFolder">ICornerTreatmentGroupFolder</see> accessors)
- **Corner5** (<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerTreatmentFeatureData">ICornerTreatmentFeatureData</see> accessors and then cast to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IComplexCornerTreatmentFeatureData">IComplexCornerTreatmentFeatureData</see>)
- more corners...
(Each corner in a complex corner group contains multiple corner members. If you edit a corner to open a Corner Management PropertyManager in the user interface, on the Complex tab are three boxes that list corner members for Trim Tool, Body Trim, and Planar Trim. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerMember">ICornerMember</see> to access these corner members.)
- **Two member Corner Group1** (ICornerTreatmentGroupFolder accessors)
- **Corner1** (ICornerTreatmentFeatureData accessors and then cast to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITwoMemberCornerTreatmentFeatureData">ITwoMemberCornerTreatmentFeatureData</see>)
- more corners...
(Each corner in a two member corner group contains two corner members, one for Trim Tool, and one for Body Trim. Use ICornerMember to access these corner members.)
- **Simple Corner Group1** (ICornerTreatmentGroupFolder accessors)
- **Corner9** (ICornerTreatmentFeatureData accessors and then cast to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISimpleCornerTreatmentFeatureData">ISimpleCornerTreatmentFeatureData</see>)
- more corners...
To create a structure system:
1. Create an <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData">IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData</see> object for every primary and secondary structure system member you intend to create.
2. Create <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemSplitMember">IStructureSystemSplitMember</see> objects as needed. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData.IsSplit">IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData::IsSplit</see> to indicate that split members exist.
3. Create one or more <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemMemberProfile">IStructureSystemMemberProfile</see> objects as the number of different profiles is needed.
4. Cast the IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData objects to <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPrimaryStructuralMemberFeatureData">IPrimaryStructuralMemberFeatureData</see> objects and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISecondaryStructuralMemberFeatureData">ISecondaryStructuralMemberFeatureData</see> objects as needed.
5. Create specific primary member feature data objects by casting IPrimaryStructuralMemberFeatureData objects to:
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPrimaryMemberFacePlaneIntersectionFeatureData">IPrimaryMemberFacePlaneIntersectionFeatureData</see> - <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPrimaryMemberPathSegmentFeatureData">IPrimaryMemberPathSegmentFeatureData</see> - <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPrimaryMemberPointLengthFeatureData">IPrimaryMemberPointLengthFeatureData</see> - <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IPrimaryMemberRefPlaneFeatureData">IPrimaryMemberRefPlaneFeatureData</see>
6. Create specific secondary member feature data objects by casting ISecondaryStructuralMemberFeatureData objects to:
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISecondaryMemberBetweenPointsFeatureData">ISecondaryMemberBetweenPointsFeatureData</see> - <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISecondaryMemberSupportPlaneFeatureData">ISecondaryMemberSupportPlaneFeatureData</see>
7. Use the methods and properties on the specific primary and secondary member feature data objects to detail the structure system members.
8. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.CreateStructureSystem">IModelDocExtension::CreateStructureSystem</see>(*primaryFDArray*, *secondaryFDArray*), where *primaryFDArray* is an array of primary IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData objects and *secondaryFDArray* is an array of secondary IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData objects created in step 1.
To edit a structure system:
1. Get the structure system folder feature, which is returned by IModelDocExtension::CreateStructureSystem in step 8 above. Then call the accessor of this interface, IFeature::GetSpecificFeature2. (Or call both accessors of this interface.)
2. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemFolder.GetProfileGroupFolders">IStructureSystemFolder::GetProfileGroupFolders</see> to access the profile group folders in a structure system folder.
3. Use IProfileGroupFolder methods and properties to get the sketch, reference plane, and structure system members in each profile group folder.
4. Use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData.StructureSystemMemberType">IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData::StructureSystemMemberType</see> to determine whether a structure system member retrieved in step 3 is a primary or a secondary member.
5. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData.AccessSelections">IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData::AccessSelections</see> before editing the selections used to create the structure system. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData.ReleaseSelectionAccess">IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData::ReleaseSelectionAccess</see> after editing.
6. Cast IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData objects to their subclass feature data objects (see create steps 5 and 6).
7. If you need to change a structure member's profile, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData.MemberProfile">IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData::MemberProfile</see> to get the IStructureSystemMemberProfile object for each structure member.
8. Complete the structure system edit by calling <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData.GetFeature">IStructureSystemMemberFeatureData::GetFeature</see>, calling methods and properties on objects retrieved in previous steps as required, and finally calling <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
Use the examples as models to create and edit structure sytems in your own applications.
For more information, read the **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Weldments and Structure System > Structure System** topics.

Type.Name: ISwColorContour1
Type.Description: Allows access to the color and display values of curvature in a SOLIDWORKS model.
Type.Remarks:
When implemented, the methods of this interface allow you to assign colors and display values of curvature in a SOLIDWORKS model.
To use ISwColorContour1:
1. Implement the ISwColorContour1 interface in an add-in class.
2. Install the implemented interface in the SOLIDWORKS software using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.InstallModelColorizer">IModelDocExtension::InstallModelColorizer</see>.
3. Run the add-in and open a model document in SOLIDWORKS.
4. In SOLIDWORKS select **View > Display > Curvature.** The model is colorized by the implemented interface.
5. When you finalize the application, remove the implemented interface from the SOLIDWORKS software using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.RemoveModelColorizer">IModelDocExtension::RemoveModelColorizer</see>.
**NOTE:** Only one color and display interface can be active at any one time. The last color and display interface installed is the active one. If you remove that color and display interface, then the color and display interface installed before it becomes the active color and display interface.
This interface overrides the color and display functionality of the SOLIDWORKS Curvature tool. See SOLIDWORKS Help for details about the SOLIDWORKS Curvature tool.
To use this interface in a SOLIDWORKS VB.NET or C# macro or add-in, see <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/OVERVIEW/ComVisibleAttribute_in_VSTA_macros.htm">ComVisibleAttribute in VB.NET and C# Macros and Add-ins</see>.

Type.Remarks:
This interface provides a callback mechanism in which:
1. SOLIDWORKS requests the partner's key through the add-in by calling <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.swpublished.ISwPEManager.IdentifyToSW">ISwPEManager::IdentifyToSW</see>,

3. SOLIDWORKS uses the license key to verify the entitlement of the SOLIDWORKS Partner and returns <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISwPEToken">ISwPEToken</see>.
See <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/GettingStarted/SolidWorks_Partner_Program_2.htm">SOLIDWORKS Partner Program</see>.

Type.Name: ISymmetricMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to symmetry mate feature data.
Type.Remarks:
Symmetry mates force two similar entities to be symmetric about a plane or planar face.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this advanced mate interface.
To create a symmetry mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISymmetricMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">ISymmetricMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1.
3. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ISymmetricMateFeatureData.SymmetryPlane">ISymmetricMateFeatureData::SymmetryPlane</see> or use IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 to pre-select the symmetry plane using Mark = 4.
4. Specify other properties of the SymmetricMateFeatureData object as required.
To edit a symmetry mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a SymmetricMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the SymmetricMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete a symmetry mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Get and Set Table Anchor of Hole Table

Type.Remarks:
If a table anchor is selected, then it can be retrieved with <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISelectionMgr.GetSelectedObject6">ISelectionMgr::GetSelectedObject6</see>. If the selected object type is swSelBOMTEMPS, then getting the selected object is a <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature">IFeature</see> object. Use <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetSpecificFeature2">IFeature::GetSpecifiedFeature2</see> to return a TableAnchor object.
If you traverse the features and subfeatures of a drawing, then the table anchors display as subfeatures of the sheet format. When <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetTypeName">IFeature::GetTypeName</see> returns GeneralTableAnchor, HoleTableAnchor, WeldmentCutListAnchor, RevisionTableAnchor, or BomTemplate, use IFeature::GetSpecificFeature2 to return a ITableAnchor object.
**NOTE:** Weld table anchors are not currently supported.
You can also retrieve a ITableAnchor object from the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISheet">ISheet</see> object using <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISheet.TableAnchor">ISheet::TableAnchor</see>. There is only one anchor of each type on a sheet format.

Type.Name: ITangentMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a tangent mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A tangent mate:
- Places selected items tangent to one another.
- Must have at least one cylindrical, conical, or spherical item.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a tangent mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITangentMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">ITangentMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities to mate using Mark = 1.
3. Specify other properties of the TangentMateFeatureData object.
To edit a tangent mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a TangentMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the TangentMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this tangent mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Description: Gains access to the text and custom properties in a <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.ThemeName">theme</see> of a <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData">SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF</see>.

Example.Name: Publish Text and Custom Properties from Theme to MBD 3D PDF
Publish Text and Custom Properties from Theme to MBD 3D PDF
Publish Text and Custom Properties from Theme to MBD 3D PDF

Type.Remarks:
SOLIDWORKS Model Based Definition (MBD) is an integrated drawingless manufacturing solution for SOLIDWORKS.
Typical steps for generating a SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using the SOLIDWORKS API are:
1. Get the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData">MBD3DPdfData object</see> using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.GetMBD3DPdfData">IModelDocExtension::GetMBD3DPdfData</see>.
2. Set the path and file name of the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF theme using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.ThemeName">IMBD3DPdfData::ThemeName</see>.
3. Get standard and custom views using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.GetStandardViews">IMBD3DPdfData::GetStandardViews</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.GetMoreViews">IMBD3DPdfData::GetMoreViews</see>.
4. Set standard and custom views using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.SetStandardViews">IMBD3DPdfData::SetStandardViews</see> and <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.SetMoreViews">IMBD3DPdfData::SetMoreViews</see>.
5. Get and set text and custom properties in the theme using the array of objects returned by this interface's accessor. See the **Accessors** section.
6. Set the path for the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMBD3DPdfData.FilePath">IMBD3DPdfData::FilePath</see>.
7. Generate the SOLIDWORKS MBD 3D PDF using <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.PublishTo3DPDF">IModelDocExtension::PublishTo3DPDF</see>.
See the SOLIDWORKS Help for details about MBD.

Type.Name: ITwoMemberCornerTreatmentFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a two member corner treatment feature of a structure system.
Type.Remarks:
This interface is:
- derived from <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerTreatmentFeatureData">ICornerTreatmentFeatureData</see>.
- valid only if <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerTreatmentFeatureData.IgnoreCornerTreatment">ICornerTreatmentFeatureData::IgnoreCornerTreatment</see> is false.
A two member corner is the position in a structure system where two members intersect. You can assign one member as a trim tool and use it to add or remove material from the other member. The trim tool member may be assigned to either member in a planar or body trim type.
In the SOLIDWORKS Design user interface, the Two member Corner PropertyManager contains three lists that you can manage using the APIs in this interface and elsewhere:
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ICornerTreatmentGroupFolder.GetCornerTreatments">Corner groups</see>
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITwoMemberCornerTreatmentFeatureData.GetCornerGroupMembers">Corner group members</see>
- <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.ITwoMemberCornerTreatmentFeatureData.MiterTrimPlanePoint">Miter trim plane point</see>
For more information, see:
- **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Weldments and Structure System > Structure System > Corner Management**
- **SOLIDWORKS Design user-interface help > Weldments and Structure System > Structure System > Two Member PropertyManager**

Type.Name: IUniversalJointMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to a universal joint mate feature.
Type.Remarks:
A universal joint (U-joint) mate consists of two components where the rotation of one component (the output shaft) about its axis is driven by the rotation of another component (the input shaft) about its axis. An example would be the U-joint between the transmission and the rear drive axle of an automobile.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this mate interface.
To create a universal joint mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IUniversalJointMateFeatureData.EntitiesToMate">IUniversalJointMateFeatureData::EntitiesToMate</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the entities using Mark = 1.
3. Set <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IUniversalJointMateFeatureData.DefineJointPoint">IUniversalJointMateFeatureData::DefineJointPoint</see> to true and specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IUniversalJointMateFeatureData.JointPoint">IUniversalJointMateFeatureData::JointPoint</see> or use IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 to pre-select the joint point using Mark = 16384.
4. Specify other properties of the UniversalJointMateFeatureData object as required.
To edit a universal joint mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a UniversalJointMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the UniversalJointMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete this universal joint mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

Type.Name: IWidthMateFeatureData
Type.Description: Allows access to width mate feature data.
Type.Remarks:
A width mate constrains a tab between two planar faces.
<see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IMateFeatureData">IMateFeatureData</see> is the parent of this advanced mate interface.
To create a width mate:
1. Follow general instructions in the <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IAssemblyDoc.CreateMate">IAssemblyDoc::CreateMate</see> Remarks.
2. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IWidthMateFeatureData.TabSelection">IWidthMateFeatureData::TabSelection</see> or use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2">IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2</see> to pre-select the tab using Mark = 16.
3. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IWidthMateFeatureData.WidthSelection">IWidthMateFeatureData::WidthSelection</see> or use IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2 to pre-select the width using Mark = 1.
4. Specify <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IWidthMateFeatureData.ConstraintType">IWidthMateFeatureData::ConstraintType</see>.
5. Specify other properties of the WidthMateFeatureData object as required.
To edit a width mate:
1. Access its feature and call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.GetDefinition">IFeature::GetDefinition</see> to get the MateFeatureData object.
2. Cast the MateFeatureData object to a WidthMateFeatureData object.
3. Modify the WidthMateFeatureData object.
4. Call <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IFeature.ModifyDefinition">IFeature::ModifyDefinition</see>.
To delete a width mate, use <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2">IModelDocExtension::DeleteSelection2</see>.

For example, in the file in the Visual C++ 6.0 wizard-generated add-in that supports SOLIDWORKS events ( <ATL_object_name>.h), include:
BEGIN_SINK_MAP(CTL_object_name>)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_SLDWORKS_EVENTS, DIID_DSldWorksEvents, swAppDocumentLoadNotify, DocumentLoadNotify)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_SLDWORKS_EVENTS, DIID_DSldWorksEvents, swAppFileNewNotify2, FileNewNotify2)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_SLDWORKS_EVENTS, DIID_DSldWorksEvents, swAppActiveDocChangeNotify, ActiveDocChangeNotify)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_SLDWORKS_EVENTS, DIID_DSldWorksEvents, swAppActiveModelDocChangeNotify, ActiveModelDocChangeNotify)
END_SINK_MAP()
If developing a C++ application, use the enumerators to <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Overview/events.htm">register for notifications</see> for the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ISldWorks">ISldWorks</see> events.

Type.Name: swBoundType_e
Type.Description: Boundary behaviors at the start and end of UV parameter ranges.
Type.Remarks: If the behavior at the start of the U range is Degenerate', then the V parameter is degenerate when U = urange[0]'. The derivative of the parameterization function with respect to v is 0 whenever u = urange[0]', for all values of v, and the parameter curve corresponding to u = urange[0]' degenerates to a single point. A parameterization can only degenerate at the end of its range, unless the surface is a B-spline surface.

Type.Name: swDrawingNotify_e

Type.Remarks:
To receive notifications, a DLL application must register for the notifications by object type. This registration must be done for each instance of a particular object.
For example, in the file in the Visual C++ 6.0 wizard-generated add-in that supports drawing events (e.g., Drawing.h), include:
BEGIN_SINK_MAP(CSwDrawing)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_DRAWINGDOC_EVENTS, DIID_DDrawingDocEvents, swDrawingDestroyNotify, DestroyNotify)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_DRAWINGDOC_EVENTS, DIID_DDrawingDocEvents, swDrawingNewSelectionNotify, NewSelectionNotify)
END_SINK_MAP()
If developing a C++ application, use the enumerators to <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Overview/events.htm">register for notifications</see> for <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IDrawingDoc">IDrawingDoc</see> events.

For example, in the file in the Visual C++ 6.0 wizard-generated add-in that supports FeatureManager design tree events (e.g., FeatMgrView.h), include:
DECLARE_REGISTRY_RESOURCEID(IDR_FeatMgrView)
BEGIN_SINK_MAP(CFeatMgrView)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_FEATMGRVIEW_EVENTS, DIID_DFeatMgrViewEvents, swFMViewDestroyNotify , DestroyNotify)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_FEATMGRVIEW_EVENTS, DIID_DFeatMgrViewEvents, swFMViewActivateNotify, ActivateNotify)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_FEATMGRVIEW_EVENTS, DIID_DFeatMgrViewEvents, swFMViewDeactivateNotify , DeActivateNotify)
END_SINK_MAP()
If developing a C++ application, use these enumerators to <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Overview/events.htm">register for notifications</see> for <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.IFeatMgrView">IFeatMgrView</see> events.

Type.Name: swPropMgrPageNumberBoxStyle_e
Type.Description: PropertyManager page number box styles. <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Overview/bitmasks.htm">Bitmask</see>.
Type.Remarks:
When the user selects an item in the attached drop-down list, SOLIDWORKS attempts to use that item as a value in the number box. Thus, the items in the attached drop-down list should be numeric values and optionally include their units. The add-in then gets a callback via IPropertyManagerPage2Handler9::OnNumberboxChanged as if the user had typed a value in the number box or clicked the up-arrow or down-arrow buttons to increment or decrement the value.
If you do not want your add-in to directly use items in the attached drop-down list in the number box, but instead want it to react to the user selecting a computed or linked value in the number box, then use swPropMgrPageNumberBoxStyle_AvoidSelectionText.

Type.Name: swSmartDimensionDirection_e
Type.Description: Smart dimension extension line directions or rapid dimensioning selector quadrants.
Type.Remarks:
In parts, this enumerator is used to specify the extension line that is needed to unambiguously define the angle to dimension. In the user interface, a direction manipulator appears during dimensioning if selected entities do not fully specify the angle to dimension. This enumerator specifies the directions of that manipulator.
In drawings that have **Rapid dimensioning** turned on, this enumerator may be used to specify the quadrant or side of the entities to which to add the display dimension.
See <see cref="SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.IModelDocExtension.AddDimension">IModelDocExtension::AddDimension</see>.

Type.Name: swTaskPaneNotify_e
Type.Description: Task Pane notifications.
Type.Remarks:
To receive notifications, a DLL application must register for the notifications by object type. This registration must be done for each instance of a particular object.
For example, in the file in the Visual C++ 6.0 wizard-generated add-in that supports Task Pane events (e.g., Taskpane.h, include:
DECLARE_REGISTRY_RESOURCEID(IDR_TaskPane)
BEGIN_SINK_MAP(CTaskPane)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_TASKPANE_EVENTS, DIID_DTaskpaneViewEvents, swAppTaskPaneDestroyNotify, DestroyNotify)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_TASKPANE_EVENTS, DIID_DTaskpaneViewEvents, swAppTaskPaneActivateNotify, ActivateNotify)
SINK_ENTRY_EX(ID_TASKPANE_EVENTS, DIID_DTaskpaneViewEvents, swAppTaskPaneDeactivateNotify, DeActivateNotify)
END_SINK_MAP()
If developing a C++ application, use these enumerators to <see href="https://help.solidworks.com/2026/english/api/sldworksapiprogguide/Overview/events.htm">register for notifications</see> for the <see cref="SOLIDWORKS.Interop.sldworks.ITaskpaneView">ITaskpaneView</see> events.
